title: The Last Colony
premise: Cyrus Ashgrove, a terraformer tending a garden on the fringe world Verdance, maintains a fragile deception: the garden is a message claiming the colony's founders still live, the only thing keeping two hostile fleets from claiming the system. When gravity stutters for nine seconds system-wide, both fleets realize someone is still transmitting—and Cyrus is exposed as the garden's sole living keeper. Hunted by both sides, Cyrus uncovers that the founders' 'inheritance' was never a weapon or a claim, but a failsafe that will render Verdance uninhabitable if either fleet lands, and that the nine-second flicker was its countdown beginning. In the end, Cyrus broadcasts the truth—that the inheritance is a choice, not a treasure—convinces a defecting officer from each fleet to stand witness, and lets the lie die so that both fleets must finally negotiate over a garden meant for people not yet born.
about_author: Dominic Lockridge is a former hydrology engineer who spent a decade writing technical manuals for remote sensing stations before turning to fiction. He lives in a coastal town where he still keeps a garden, and insists the two hobbies are the same thing.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Silence
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. During routine maintenance in the founder's garden, gravity across the entire system stutters for exactly nine seconds, killing the irrigation grid. Cyrus restarts it by hand and tells no one. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine—the sense that something vast just noticed them.

chapters.title: The Garden for the Unborn
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, with a flashback. We learn the garden is a living broadcast: its soil chemistry, tree rings, and pollen signature transmit a coded claim that the founding generation still lives. Emotional beat: tenderness and fraud intertwined—Cyrus loves a garden that is also a lie.

chapters.title: Long Route Between Worlds
chapters.summary: Cyrus pilots the supply run between Verdance and the relay moon Halcyon, passing through the demilitarized corridor between the Meridian Fleet and the Ashfall Compact. Emotional beat: loneliness of the middle path; Cyrus is the only traffic in a corridor built for war.

chapters.title: What the Relay Heard
chapters.summary: Halcyon technician Sefa Okonjo's POV. Sefa detects that the nine-second gravity event registered identically on both fleets' instruments—and that both fleets have quietly reopened queries about Verdance. Emotional beat: the itch of a pattern that shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Ash
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In the founder's sealed archive, Cyrus rereads the inheritance protocol: if either fleet lands, the garden triggers a terraforming collapse. Cyrus has kept this secret for eleven years. Emotional beat: the weight of a secret that has become a personality.

chapters.title: The Meridian Inquiry
chapters.summary: Meridian Fleet Captain Ilse Varga's POV. Ordered to investigate the gravity anomaly, Varga dispatches a survey ship toward Verdance, officially routine. Emotional beat: professional unease—Varga suspects her orders are someone else's gambit.

chapters.title: Rootstock
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A survey probe lands at the garden's edge. Cyrus scrambles to make the garden read as 'continuously tended by many hands,' forging decades of maintenance logs in the founders' voices. Emotional beat: desperate craftsmanship; lying in the medium Cyrus knows best.

chapters.title: The Compact's Question
chapters.summary: Ashfall Compact officer Dario Ren's POV. Ren, an intelligence analyst, has spent years disbelieving the Verdance claim. The gravity event gives him his opening to demand an expedition. Emotional beat: ambition sharpened into obsession.

chapters.title: Letters to No One
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus writes the monthly 'founders' broadcast,' impersonating voices dead for sixty years—including, sometimes, the voice of Cyrus's own grandmother. Emotional beat: grief disguised as duty; the lie has become a séance.

chapters.title: Halcyon intermediary
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Cyrus asks Sefa to delay relaying the gravity anomaly data to both fleets. Sefa agrees but keeps a copy. Emotional beat: the first crack in Cyrus's isolation—trust extended, leverage created.

chapters.title: The Survey Ship Arrives
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Meridian's survey vessel Halcyon's Reach enters orbit. Its commander, Lt. Ansel Breck, requests a landing tour. Cyrus must host the enemy inside the lie. Emotional beat: performance under pressure, terror masked as hospitality.

chapters.title: Breck's Doubt
chapters.summary: Ansel Breck's POV. Breck finds the garden moving and beautiful but the maintenance logs subtly wrong—too consistent, too literary. He says nothing in his report. Emotional beat: conscience versus career; a man choosing what not to see.

chapters.title: The Compact Lands
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Dario Ren's expedition arrives uninvited, weeks ahead of any schedule, forcing Cyrus to improvise a second performance for a sharper audience. Emotional beat: the noose tightening; two predators in one garden.

chapters.title: Ren's Interrogation
chapters.summary: Dario Ren's POV. Ren interviews Cyrus and notices the pronoun problem—the founders' logs use 'we,' but everything is singular in its care. Emotional beat: the hunter's pleasure of almost-confirmation.

chapters.title: Gravity Flickers Again
chapters.summary: Multiple POV interlude. A second, shorter flicker hits—seven seconds this time. Both fleets interpret it as a signal. Sefa realizes the intervals are counting down. Emotional beat: systemic dread; the universe is speaking in a language of physics.

chapters.title: The Failsafe Hypothesis
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Working from relay archives, Sefa reconstructs the founders' failsafe and realizes Verdance itself is the countdown clock. Sefa sends Cyrus a warning—and keeps a copy for both fleets' rivals. Emotional beat: the terrible arithmetic of a whistleblower.

chapters.title: House of Roots
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus begins sabotaging the garden to slow the countdown, killing parts of a living thing Cyrus has raised for decades. Emotional beat: sacrilege; to save the lie, Cyrus must wound the truth.

chapters.title: Varga's Gambit
chapters.summary: Captain Varga's POV. Varga, suspecting the Compact will seize Verdance, moves her fleet to the corridor edge—officially a drill. Emotional beat: a commander gambling her career on a hunch that the prize is a trap.

chapters.title: The Broadcast That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Both fleets receive a 'founders' transmission' Cyrus never sent—someone is forging the forger. Emotional beat: vertigo; the lie has escaped its author.

chapters.title: Sefa's Price
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa is detained by Compact security for data irregularities and bargains: freedom for the full failsafe analysis. Emotional beat: fear and resolve; the middleman becomes a hostage.

chapters.title: What Cyrus Buried
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, deep flashback. We learn Cyrus's grandmother was the last founder, that she built the failsafe, and that she made eleven-year-old Cyrus promise to keep the garden 'alive until they come home.' Emotional beat: inheritance as wound; loyalty installed before understanding.

chapters.title: The Corridor Closes
chapters.summary: Varga and Ren POVs interleaved. Both fleets declare emergency posture; the demilitarized corridor is sealed with Cyrus's next supply run scheduled mid-seal. Emotional beat: the long route is now a trap with Cyrus inside it.

chapters.title: Run the Corridor
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A white-knuckle transit through the closed corridor, hailing both fleets with forged credentials, carrying Sefa's warning data. Emotional beat: courage as momentum—Cyrus stops deciding and simply moves.

chapters.title: Ren's Revelation
chapters.summary: Dario Ren's POV. Ren decrypts the founders' archive and confirms the failsafe: landing means mutual destruction of the colony's value. He reports it—and is ordered to land anyway, as proof the Compact won't be blackmailed. Emotional beat: ideology devouring its own believer.

chapters.title: Varga Refuses
chapters.summary: Captain Varga's POV. Ordered to beat the Compact to the surface, Varga instead requests parley, citing the failsafe. She is relieved of command. Emotional beat: integrity's cost; the right order from the wrong position.

chapters.title: The Garden Burns
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Compact landing parties torch the perimeter to force compliance; the countdown accelerates as the failsafe reads assault. Cyrus watches forty years of growth burn. Emotional beat: devastation; the lie dies in fire, and something truer is exposed in the ash.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds, Final Draft
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV, freed amid the chaos. The final flicker will last nine seconds—and during it, every failsafe in the system can be disarmed by a single broadcast from the garden's root array. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: The Truth Broadcast
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. From the burning garden, Cyrus hijacks the founders' array and broadcasts everything: the founders are dead, the garden is one person's work, the failsafe is real, and the inheritance is a choice. Emotional beat: liberation through confession; the lie's last act is honesty.

chapters.title: Breck Chooses
chapters.summary: Ansel Breck's POV. Breck, ordered to silence the broadcast, instead lands and stands beside Cyrus, declaring himself witness. Emotional beat: a small act of defection that changes the geometry of the standoff.

chapters.title: Ren's Crisis
chapters.summary: Dario Ren's POV. Facing the truth broadcast and his own orders, Ren must choose between the Compact's doctrine and the evidence of his own eyes. Emotional beat: the collapse of a certainty he built his life on.

chapters.title: The Countdown
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. With minutes left, Cyrus, Breck, and a defecting Compact tech race through the burning root array to arm the disarm-broadcast before the final flicker. Emotional beat: climax—every skill Cyrus used to lie now spent to tell the truth in time.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Truth
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The final flicker hits; the disarm broadcast fires; both fleets' failsafe triggers go dark. In nine seconds of weightlessness, the system holds its breath. Emotional beat: stillness at the peak—war postponed by physics and one stubborn gardener.

chapters.title: Parley at Verdance
chapters.summary: Varga's POV, reinstated ad hoc. With the failsafe disarmed but the truth public, both fleets must talk. Varga brokers a parley on Verdance's scorched edge. Emotional beat: exhausted diplomacy; enemies meeting on ground neither can claim.

chapters.title: The Terms of Soil
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus addresses the parley—not as a founder's heir but as the garden's only gardener—and proposes joint stewardship: the colony belongs to whoever tends it, not whoever claims it. Emotional beat: redefining inheritance from possession to obligation.

chapters.title: Ren's Testimony
chapters.summary: Dario Ren's POV. Ren testifies against his own expedition's orders, burning his career to legitimize the parley. Emotional beat: costly redemption; the skeptic becomes the truth's most credible witness.

chapters.title: What Grows Back
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, months later. First rains after the burns; crews from both fleets plant together under a provisional charter. Cyrus teaches, no longer alone. Emotional beat: grief and renewal braided; the garden becomes what it always claimed to be.

chapters.title: Sefa's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa publishes the complete archive—the lies, the failsafe, the flickers—refusing to let any side own the story. Emotional beat: the ethics of memory; truth as infrastructure.

chapters.title: Letters to Someone
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus writes a final entry in the founders' log, this time in Cyrus's own voice, for the children of the joint colony. Emotional beat: the séance ends; the living speak in their own names.

chapters.title: The Long Route, Open
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The corridor reopens under joint administration, and Cyrus runs the route again—now busy, now shared. Emotional beat: the middle path becomes the main road; isolation resolved into belonging.

chapters.title: The Garden for the Born
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, closing chapter. Years on, children born under the charter work the beds Cyrus once tended alone. The gravity is steady. Cyrus plants a tree with no message in it at all. Emotional beat: quiet fulfillment—an inheritance finally given as a garden, not a lie.
